{
  "units": [
    {
      "title": "Course Overview – Basics of Java",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0001"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The course will teach the basics of Java.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Course Overview – Java Execution",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0002"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The course will teach how Java code gets executed.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Course Overview – Simple Algorithms",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0003"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The course will teach how to build simple algorithms.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Tool Installation – Prerequisites",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0004"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The course will cover installing all the necessary tools to build Java applications.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "JDK Definition",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0005"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "JDK stands for Java Development Kit and is a software development environment for building Java applications.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "JDK Components",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0006"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The JDK includes a compiler, reusable code libraries, and a Java runtime environment.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Official JDK Download Source",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0007"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Oracle.com provides the Java SE (Standard Edition) download page for the JDK.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Platform Availability",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0008"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The JDK can be downloaded for various platforms such as Linux, macOS, and Windows.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "macOS Distribution Format",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0009"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "On macOS, the JDK is provided as a .dmg file.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "License Acceptance",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0010"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Installation of the JDK requires accepting the license agreement.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "macOS Installation Wizard Steps",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0011"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The JDK installation wizard on macOS guides the user through clicking continue, entering the computer password, and completing the installation.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Popular Java Editors",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0016"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Popular code editors for building Java applications are NetBeans, Eclipse, and IntelliJ.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Instructor’s Preferred Editor",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0017"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The instructor’s favorite editor can be used for the course.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0018"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition is free and sufficient for the course.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Application Placement on macOS",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0019"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "After downloading, the application should be dragged into the Applications folder.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Fundamental Building Block – Functions",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0020"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The smallest building block in Java programs are functions.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Function Definition",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0021"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "A function is a block of code that performs a task.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Analogy – Remote Control Buttons",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0022"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Each button on a remote control performs a task, analogous to functions in programming.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Analogy – Functions as Buttons",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0023"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Functions in programming languages are analogous to remote control buttons.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Function Examples",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0024"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Examples of functions include sending emails, converting weight units, and validating user input.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Coding a Function in Java",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0025"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The tutorial will demonstrate how to code a function in Java.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Return Type Position",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0026"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The return type of a function is specified first.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Return Types – Value vs None",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0027"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Some functions return a value like a number or a date/time, while other functions do not return anything.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Void Return Type",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0028"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The return type of functions that do not return a value is void.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Void Keyword",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0029"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Void is a reserved keyword in Java.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Function Name Placement",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0030"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "After the return type, the name of the function appears.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Descriptive Function Names",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0031"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "A function should have a descriptive name, such as send email.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Purpose‑Clear Naming",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0032"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "The function name clearly identifies its purpose.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Parameter List Syntax",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0033"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "After the function name, parentheses contain the parameters for the function.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Parameter Role",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0034"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Parameters are used to pass values to a function.",
      "visuals": []
    },
    {
      "title": "Example Parameters for sendEmail",
      "source_segment_ids": ["FCT_0035"],
      "mode": "text_only",
      "remaining_text": "Example parameters for a send email function include the receiver, subject, and content of the email.",
      "visuals": []
    }]}
